title: Dismantle assets
goal: An item broken down rather than sold whole has its hazardous pieces removed first, its usable parts recorded with where they are kept, and its own record closed so the register no longer shows a whole machine.

steps.do: Say why the item is being broken down rather than sold or recycled whole, what must come out first and in what order (battery, drive, refrigerant, fuel, capacitors), who is qualified to remove each, and what tools and protection the work needs.

consider.why: Taking the wrong part out first is how a dismantling job becomes a fire, a spill or a data loss.
consider.when: The venture is breaking down physical equipment for parts instead of selling or recycling it whole.

steps.do: Record which parts are kept for reuse, which go to recycling and which are waste, with where each kept part is stored, and register any kept part that is itself worth tracking (a drive, a battery pack, a tool head) as its own item.

consider.why: Parts that are not recorded when they come out are parts the venture buys again six months later.
consider.when: The dismantled item yields parts worth keeping or parts that must be disposed of separately.

steps.do: Close the dismantled item's record with the disposal date, the method, whether its data-holding parts were wiped or destroyed, and a note naming the parts kept from it, so the register shows parts rather than a machine.
Attach what the dismantling recovered and what it cost to the decision that approved it, and raise to the founder any part that needs a licensed handler before it can leave.

done_criteria.check: Is every dismantled item's record closed with its disposal and the parts kept from it named, and was each part that holds data or is hazardous handled before anything else came out?
